purpose: Extend the prior frozen IR baseline with finite single-CPU/single-GPU request lifecycle, asynchronous serving, PD handoff and expert scheduling requirements.
freeze_policy: Requirements and denominators are fixed before implementing these adapters. Unsupported or unverified cases remain in their group denominators. The prior 38-case manifest is unchanged and evaluated separately.
scope: Exactly one CPU and one GPU in one shared ModelPlan -> IR -> compiler -> modeling runtime; explicit finite arrivals and decode traces; Dense and trace-driven MoE; DRAM/VRAM capacities, shared cache and cross-layer prefetch; independently declared synthetic kernel/transfer prices.
excluded: fused dynamic-batch kernel performance unless independently and explicitly priced
oracle_policy: Write expected lifecycle times, identities, dependencies, bytes and causal boundaries before compilation. Compiler output is observed evidence only. Require goal_reached for positive/combination runs; a valid prefix is insufficient. Synthetic time changes are declared inputs, never measurements or fitted hardware claims.

positive.name: Request arrival and retirement
positive.requirement: Declare at least two requests with distinct arrival times and unequal finite decode lengths; requests join and retire independently in one runtime.
positive.oracle: No request-specific operation, activation/KV allocation or compute is visible/issued before its arrival; each intended invocation executes exactly once; the shorter request has no subsequent compute; final retirement does not reset other requests or duplicate weights.

positive.name: Asynchronous decode dependencies
positive.requirement: Allow a request's next decode round once its own preceding round completes, without waiting for every other request to finish the corresponding round.
positive.oracle: Positive-duration next-round work overlaps another request's earlier-round work when dependencies/resources permit; every same-request layer/round dependency is preserved; all declared rounds complete once.

positive.name: Request execution pipeline
positive.requirement: Run CPU Attention and GPU FFN for independently scheduled requests under one high-level declaration and one resource ledger.
positive.oracle: At least one positive-duration cross-request CPU Attention/GPU FFN compute overlap; per-request producer dependencies and all tensor transfer payloads are correct; one clock and shared capacities.

positive.name: Explicit batch accounting
positive.requirement: An invocation containing two requests declares independent per-request kernels and exact batch-axis cost entries; no measured whole-batch duration is silently reused or divided.
positive.oracle: Fresh synthetic physical signatures explicitly identify invocation_batch=2 and kernel_batch=1/request accounting; each intended kernel is charged once with its exact price; prices with batch=1 cannot satisfy batch=2 lookup.

positive.name: Full-layer PD KV handoff
positive.requirement: Prefill all layers on GPU, then hand the request's complete per-layer KV history to CPU Decode with explicit data movement and a phase handoff dependency.
positive.oracle: Every layer/token KV identity and payload is preserved, each required GPU-to-CPU KV copy is charged exactly once, and no Decode computation starts before the declared complete handoff; history subsequently grows correctly.

positive.name: Revealed-route expert scheduling
positive.requirement: Choose CPU/GPU expert execution from current public routes and history after route revelation; expert cache/prefetch must respect the same physical inventory.
positive.oracle: Every expert compute corresponds to an already revealed route, each expert region has complete inputs/results, payloads are charged, and the finite workload reaches its goal.

combinations.name: Lifecycle + asynchronous pipeline
combinations.requirement: Distinct arrivals and unequal decode lengths coexist with actual cross-request CPU/GPU overlap and asynchronous next-round progress in one runtime.
combinations.oracle: All S01/S02 lifecycle/dependency conditions plus actual S03 overlap; no new session or cache per request.

combinations.name: PD handoff + shared cache/prefetch
combinations.requirement: All-layer PD handoff composes with bounded shared weight caching and a real cross-layer prefetch while work is active.
combinations.oracle: All S05 KV bytes/dependencies; at least one audited speculative COPY overlapping active prior-layer computation; shared cache including reservations and physical capacities never overflow.

combinations.name: Expert scheduling + cache/prefetch
combinations.requirement: Trace-driven MoE routing, CPU/GPU expert choices, expert cache reuse and cross-layer prefetch execute together.
combinations.oracle: Revealed-route boundaries preserved; at least one reused physical expert weight needs no redundant reload; real speculative COPY and compute/transfer costs; one bounded cache ledger and complete inference.

combinations.name: Lifecycle + PD + experts
combinations.requirement: Two arriving requests with unequal decode lengths use MoE, all-layer PD handoff, causal expert scheduling and shared bounded cache in a single compiled plan/runtime.
combinations.oracle: All lifecycle, round, route and handoff invariants hold together; no request reset, route leak, early Decode, duplicate uncharged weight inventory or separate-runtime substitution; complete goal.

negative.name: Unarrived request execution
negative.requirement: Reject an action targeting a request's operation before its declared arrival for the explicit arrival/visibility reason; treating it as a supported ready operation is forbidden.

negative.name: Premature PD decode
negative.requirement: Reject a request's Decode COMPUTE before complete Prefill and declared all-layer KV handoff; isolate the handoff/dependency failure rather than an unrelated unavailable device or missing weight.

negative.name: Mismatched batch price
negative.requirement: Reject a two-request invocation whose required batch=2 exact cost entry is absent/replaced with batch=1; no interpolation, duplication, silent division or free zero cost.

negative.name: Unrevealed future expert execution
negative.requirement: Reject targeting an expert region before its invocation route is public for the information-boundary reason, even when the static weight catalogue lists that expert.

causal.name: Private future arrivals
causal.requirement: Compare two workloads with identical public request/resource history up to a boundary but different later request arrivals/lengths.
causal.oracle: Nonempty canonical public observation/decision prefixes before the first differing revelation are identical, including shared cache/prefetch behavior; both complete workloads independently reach their goals. A policy must not receive private arrival futures.

causal.name: Private future expert routes
causal.requirement: Compare two MoE traces identical up to a route revelation and different in the later expert assignment under the same lifecycle/PD/resource conditions.
causal.oracle: Nonempty canonical public observation/decision prefixes before the first differing route revelation are identical; no future expert task is publicly executable; both full workloads complete with their own revealed expert assignments.

status_policy.pass: All independently specified obligations checked; positive/combination/causal runs reach the complete goal.
status_policy.fail: A supported declaration violates a required observable invariant or a negative case is accepted/rejected for the wrong reason.
status_policy.unsupported: The required serving mechanism is not implemented. This remains a coverage gap, never a passing negative.
status_policy.unverified: Execution or oracle evidence is incomplete; no passing claim.
status_policy.policy_dead_end: A policy cannot advance; does not establish global infeasibility.
